title: Prepayment and Re-amortization Terms of the Equipment & Vehicle Loans Note
content:
**Terms.** Principal of an Equipment & Vehicle Loans loan may be prepaid at any time. A prepayment fee applies only to a fixed-rate loan whose original principal is at or above the product's prepayment fee threshold: principal prepaid in a loan year beyond the product's free prepayment percentage of original principal (counting earlier prepayments of the same loan year) carries the fee percentage of the prepayment fee schedule entry for the current loan year, rounded to cents, booked as a prepayment fee pointing to the principal payment it is charged on. Prepayments by release proceeds of a sale count toward the allowance and the fee; proceeds of a total-loss insurance settlement and principal paid as part of scheduled installments never do. A variable-rate loan, and every product with an empty schedule, has no prepayment fee. A prepayment shortens the schedule and leaves the installment unchanged, unless the member asks to re-amortize: re-amortization is offered only when the product's re-amortization minimum is above zero and principal prepaid or paid from release proceeds since funding or the last re-amortization is at least that amount; the new installment amortises the principal balance over the installments remaining to the maturity date at the contract rate, and the product's re-amortization fee is assessed.

## The fee as a figure

The free amount still available in a loan year is the original principal multiplied by the free prepayment percentage and divided by 100, rounded to cents, less the prepayments already counted in that loan year, and never below zero. The chargeable part of a prepayment is the prepayment less that free amount, never below zero. The prepayment fee is the chargeable part multiplied by the schedule's fee percentage for the current loan year and divided by 100, rounded to cents.

**Hypothetical worked example.** A fixed-rate New Equipment Loan of 300000.00 original principal (threshold 250000, free prepayment 20 %) in loan year 2: the free amount for the year is 60000.00; 50000.00 was prepaid earlier in the same loan year, leaving 10000.00 free. A new prepayment of 30000.00 has a chargeable part of 20000.00, which at the loan-year-2 entry of 2.0 % carries a fee of 400.00.

## What counts toward the allowance and the fee

| Principal paid | Counts toward allowance and fee |
|---|---|
| Voluntary prepayment | yes |
| Release proceeds of a sale | yes |
| Proceeds of a total-loss insurance settlement | never |
| Principal paid as part of scheduled installments | never |

## Re-amortization

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| The product's re-amortization minimum is zero | re-amortization is not offered |
| Minimum above zero, prepaid or release-paid principal since funding or the last re-amortization below it | not offered |
| Minimum above zero, that principal at or above it, member asks | new installment amortising the principal balance over the installments remaining to maturity at the contract rate; re-amortization fee assessed |
| Member does not ask | the schedule shortens and the installment stays unchanged |

## Points of judgement

- A fixed-rate loan below the threshold, a variable-rate loan and any product with an empty schedule carry no prepayment fee.
- Hypothetical: on a Used Equipment Loan (minimum 10000) with 9500.00 prepaid since funding the member cannot yet re-amortize; at 10000.00 the member may.
